chunks: From him, from his father, from Al-Qasim ibn 'Urwa, from 'Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
There is no problem with wearing silk (al-qazz) when its warp or its flesh (weft/body) is mixed with cotton or flax.

key_terms.الْقَزِّ: Silk (specifically referring to the fabric or fiber)
key_terms.سَدَاهُ: Its warp (the longitudinal threads in weaving)
key_terms.لَحْمَتُهُ: Its flesh/body (referring to the weft or the main substance of the fabric)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to wear silk if it is mixed with cotton or flax?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the juristic distinction between pure silk and mixed fabrics, affirming that men may wear silk provided it is blended with permissible natural fibers like cotton or flax. It specifically addresses the structural integrity of the weave, ruling that if the silk forms the warp (sada) or the main body (lahma), the garment remains valid for male wearers, reflecting the Shia emphasis on practical textile composition over absolute prohibition.

en.hubeali:
From him, from his father, from Al Qasim Bin Urwa, from Ubeyd Bin Zurara, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:
‘There is no problem with Al-Qazz (silk) clothes when it was either seamed or united with the cotton or flax’.
en.sarwar: 10. it is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from his father from al-Qasim ibn ‘Urwah from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
It is not unlawful to use a garments which are made of al-Qazz if its warp or weft is of cotton or kattan (linen, the fibers of certain plants).”’
